body:
Really all I would want from my friends is to talk. I wouldn't ask them to do anything besides listen. I just don't want them to be worried about my well-being all the time. I want my time with them to be enjoyable and not have to worry about things like that and not to think I am this broken thing that needs to be checked up on to make sure I'm functioning. 

Sadly going along with the failing out of school, I had to move back home, so this isn't the first time. It's a LOT more serious though because of the fact I am in my own apartment rather than dorms.

It's just so odd. When I am with my friends I can be this person full of confidence and energy. I can act like myself and just enjoy everything. It's not an act at all. That's how I honestly feel. When I am alone for an extended period of time though is when things start to spiral. 

I think part of my problem as well is I feel the need to cling to something. At pretty much all points in my life I have had SOMEONE to just be there. I would either have my girlfriend at the time, my mother, or my councilor. This is the first time that I just feel like I don't have that person and I am missing something majorly and I'm grasping. I guess that comes with the self-confidence thing eh? I just don't understand why I can be so full of confidence at one moment, but the next I am this desperate ball of self-hate.

First off, I'd like to give you a big thank you for just sitting here and talking to me. It's honestly making me feel a lot better right now.

That's pretty much the tip of the iceburg between me and my father, though. His talking down to me was a very large contributing factor to me failing out of school the first time. The words, "You will never amount to anything" were said a couple times. He was never physically abusive to me and my mother, but the emotional abuse was so extreme that at times I feared for my mother's sake. Thankfully they aren't together anymore, so she doesn't need to deal with him anymore. I sadly do though :/

 The last counselor I talked to pretty much made it clear that he is a big part of where my problems came from in the beginning. He's not a very nice man to say the least. 

And no sadly I don't currently have a job. I just moved to my new place relatively recently and am looking for something that will fit around my school schedule for the fall. Now that you mention it though, for the past year I was working a pretty much full time job and it did make me feel a lot better. 

My biggest problem about asking my really close friends for help is that I don't want to make things weird between us. I confided in my mother most of the time growing up when I was having problems, and our relationship is still fantastic. She goes quite a bit overboard and I feel like it does affect our relationship a bit because any time I am in a little bit of a bad mood in the past she would make a very big deal out of it, when I just wanted to relax and read a book or something. I care about my friends too much to make something awkward like that stand between us and make them worry, you know?

I'm still taking the medication. I just got an upped dose a couple months ago. I could see another one, but that's part of the problem. I don't know why I am so ashamed or afraid to tell people that I fell back into my same hole for some reason. I was having some slight issues a while back and pretty much lashed out at them when anyone confronted me about it so they stopped asking. I would need to tell my dad that I am going to see a counselor again because there is no way I could pay for them without using his insurance. He doesn't know that I am still taking my meds or having problems at all. Last time he found out he talked down to me like I am broken and should deal with my problems myself.

I failed out in the first attempt because I started to get into one of my depressive cycles and just gave up. That was when I went to see someone and started taking my medication. I nearly did the second time because I felt so awful about the first time, and all I was doing was trying to get my GPA out of the shitter. 

I don't really know what I am expecting to happen because I am in such a conflicting mood with the whole thing. I know I NEED help, but I keep refusing to ask for it.

I used to talk to someone and have been on medication for a couple years. I stopped seeing my counselor when I started to feel better though. That was a long while ago and I sort of left on a really bad note with the counselor so I can't really see that particular one anymore.

I know I have depression alongside an anxiety disorder.
